fact: CIPESA lists Guinea, with Burkina Faso, Lesotho, Mali, Namibia and Uganda, as still at different stages in developing its AI policy or strategy; no adoption is stated. No date of its own is given, so the document's published date is used.
The ministry (MPTEN) reports that in 2025 a national AI roadmap 2026-2035 was validated and a three-phase strategy to master and regulate AI was adopted, with UNDP's AILA methodology.

Guinea's ICT ministry said on 20 December 2025 that it validated a national AI roadmap for 2026-2035 after a 19 December workshop with UNDP; the source reports validation and no adoption or launch by the government.

Guinea's higher-education ministry and the Cité des Sciences et de l'Innovation are applying the UN Blueprint for national AI strategies, and the next steps are sector consultations and finalising the national strategy document.

A validation workshop held by the Ministry of Posts, Telecommunications and Digital Economy with UNDP ended with the final AILA diagnostic report and a ten-year national AI roadmap for 2026 to 2035 officially handed over.
